text: Buy her flour before she asks.
Tell her the corner shop could be hers.
Put her name to the empty storefront.
Walk her through the rebuilt shop.
Put your own name to the storefront.
Take the rebuilt shop for yourself.
Sell her flour at the price she'll pay.
Tell her there's nothing here for her.
Put three against what he owes.
Ask about his daughter, and listen.
Say the coast would suit him.
Help him pack the shop up.
Mention to his creditor that he's behind.
Buy his stock at what he'll take.
He is sitting on the step. He doesn't look up.
Buy his tools back out of pawn.
Stand in the ruin and tell him it can be rebuilt.
Find him the first small job.
Hire his hands out and keep the difference.
Tell him the ruin is coming down.
Splice the fraying rope for her.
Draw the day's water before she wakes.
Sell her a length of rope at your price.
Tell her the rope will hold another winter.
Walk his round with him.
Take the cold end of his round again.
Doze in his lantern-light and let him walk.
Report that he sleeps on the wall.
Thread her needles for the week.
Sit and thread for her again.
Buy her last good coat cheap.
Tell her customers her stitching has gone.
Help him tar the leak in his boat.
Bail with him before the tide.
Take his morning catch on credit you won't pay.
Cut his mooring line loose in the night.
Split a week of firewood for her.
Stack another cord against her wall.
Take her husband's tools; she won't use them.
Tell her the house is wanted by someone else.
Walk the ditches with him calling for his dog.
Call for the dog again, further out.
Sell him a story about where the dog went.
Tell him the dog is dead. It isn't.
Give him the chalk you were saving.
Sit with the slow ones while he teaches.
Sell the school's last books for what they'll fetch.
Tell the parents he drinks.
Walk her home from the far farms.
Take the lantern and walk her out again.
Charge her for the lantern oil.
Let her walk the dark road alone.
Take two barrels off his hands.
Buy another barrel you don't need.
Haggle him down below his cost.
Tell the brewer his barrels leak.
Bring her the good salve for her hands.
Turn the mangle for her an hour.
Pay her late, and less.
Say the linen came back grey.
Sit with him over his father's ledgers.
Take a share of the debt onto your name.
Buy the forge tools at a widow's price.
Tell the creditors where the tools are kept.
Help her move the failing hives to the sun.
Carry the frames out for her again.
Take a jar of the last honey for nothing.
Leave the hive lids off overnight.
Help him drag the boat over the low bar.
Pull the rope with him again at dusk.
Cross without paying; he won't ask twice.
Tell travellers the ferry has stopped running.
Sweep out her empty rooms with her.
Sit in her empty room so it isn't empty.
Take a bed and a meal, and settle later.
Tell the carters her beds have lice.
Stay late and help him finish the wheel.
Hold the rim while he sets the tyre.
Take the wheel he made for someone else.
Tell his customer the order will not come.
Stand in her doorway where people can see you.
Buy from her in front of the others.
Take her remedy and pay her in talk.
Repeat what they say about her, louder.
Help him spread the spoiled hemp to dry.
Turn the hemp with him again.
Buy his good rope for the price of the bad.
Tell the boatmen his rope is rotten.
Sit the night watch on the high field.
Take the cold watch again.
Take a kid from the herd; she's lost count.
Leave the gate open behind you.
Carry the stone he can't lift any more.
Shoulder his load again, and say nothing.
Take the job he's too slow for now.
Say his walls are coming down.
Bring her tallow from your own store.
Bring her tallow again.
Buy her candles cheap and sell them dear.
Tell her buyers her candles smoke.
Help him find a way round the washed-out road.
Walk the long way with him again.
Take his beasts' grazing for your own.
Send him down the road that's gone.
Help her re-lay the cracked kiln.
Pack the kiln with her again.
Take the pots that survived, for nothing.
Tell her the clay here was always bad.
Climb up and re-hang the bell rope.
Ring the hours for him.
Take the lead off the roof; no one looks up.
Let the bell stay silent and say nothing.
Help her true the warped loom.
Wind her bobbins for the evening.
Take the cloth she wove for another.
Tell the market her cloth runs short.
Help him dress the millstone.
Turn the stone with him again.
Take your flour and settle at harvest, maybe.
Say his flour has grit in it.
Bail out her flooded cellar.
Carry the wheels up out of the wet.
Take the cheese that's still good.
Tell them her cellar is fouled.
Cut reeds with him while there's light.
Bundle the reeds with him again.
Have him thatch yours first, and pay last.
Tell the village his roofs let water.
Read the labels aloud until she knows them.
Sit and read the hard ones again.
Let her guess, and buy what she mislabels.
Tell the apothecary she can't read.
Help him move the pits downwind.
Dig with him again at the new pits.
Buy his leather at the price the smell allows.
Complain about the smell where it carries.
Help her sort the glass that survived.
Sweep the broken glass with her again.
Take the whole panes for your own window.
Say she broke the shipment herself.
Speak for him about the closed forest.
Speak for him again, to someone who matters.
Buy his last charcoal for nothing.
Agree that the forest should stay shut.
Bring her wool from your own back.
Bring her what wool you can spare.
Take her yarn and pay her in thanks.
Tell them her yarn breaks.
Bring your horse to him, not the town smith.
Bring the neighbour's horse to him too.
Take a shoeing and forget to pay.
Say his nails lame the horses.
Cut willow with her by the river.
Strip the willow with her again.
Take a basket each time you pass.
Cut the willow stand back to nothing.
Help him re-hang the loose axe head.
Swing with him until the cord is cut.
Take his cut wood; he'll blame the road.
Leave the head loose and say it's fine.
Sit up with the dry cow through the night.
Sit up with her again.
Take the last of the milk for yourself.
Tell the farmer she let the cow go dry.
Hold the glass steady while he works.
Hold the light for him again.
Buy the clock his hands can't finish.
Say his clocks all run slow.
Sit and mend net with her.
Mend the long net with her again.
Take a net and settle after the season.
Tell the boats her nets part.
Write to the town about his pension.
Write again, and this time sign it.
Drink what's left of his pension with him.
Tell them he was never in the regiment.
